incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for /v1/generate (canary=20% traffic) — p99=3.8s (SLO=2.0s). Triggered at 2026-03-14T15:12:35Z. Paging prod-oncall and infra-oncall :rotating_light:

sanjay: saw the bot — is this from the new model rollout? canary is 20% yes

maeve: yep new model v2.3.0 started ramp at 15:00, shadowing for 10m then started 20% traffic at ~15:08

olivia: quick check: p95 jumped too but not as much. p95=1.9s, p99=3.8s. streaming stalls on a subset of requests (long context).

infra-oncall: looking at GPU hosts - some increased kernel scheduler wait. no OOMs. pulling logs now.

prod-oncall: customer-success FYI this might hit a few customers on streaming. any live complaints?

customer-success: two enterprise customers reported degraded streaming in the last 10m, one on Dedicated but using canary config for testing. escalating to their AE.

sanjay: mitigation proposal: 1) pause canary ramp, 2) route canary traffic to stable model variant, 3) run diagnostic trace on offending requests. agree?

maeve: +1. also capture tail traces and stack on runtime. enable verbose kv-cache logs for canary group only.

olivia: working on tracer. adding rule to sampler to capture >2.5s tails: `rb-trace --service=inference --filter "latency>2500" --out=/tmp/canary-tail.traces`

infra-oncall: temporarily bumped canary pool from 3 -> 6 replicas to see if it's load-dependent. scaling command ran:  
```
kubectl scale deploy/ri-canary-v2 --replicas=6 -n inference
```
replicas are coming up (3/6 ready)

prod-oncall: executing pause ramp and traffic shift to stable:  
```
redwoodctl rollout pause --env=prod --target=canary-v2
redwoodctl routing set --route=/v1/generate --group=stable --percent=100
```

incident-bot: ACTION_LOG: rollout paused by prod-oncall at 15:15:12Z; routing changed to stable at 15:15:18Z.

maeve: after shift, p99 dropped to 2.1s within 90s but still above 2.0. p95 is 1.1s. looks like tail is improving but not fully recovered.

sanjay: good. keep stable at 100% while we triage. we need to understand root cause: model behavior vs runtime path. can we repro locally?

olivia: reproducer: longer prompts (>=2048 tokens) with streaming + tool calling seem to hit stall when KV cache miss pattern is unusual. adding sample trace:  
```
[2026-03-14T15:13:05Z] req=abcd123 latency=3800ms stage=kv-lookup file=kvcache.cpp:132
[2026-03-14T15:13:05Z] req=abcd123 warning=async-kv-timeout retry=1
[2026-03-14T15:13:06Z] stage=attention kernel=matmul slow-path
```
suggests some requests take a slow-path in kernels with larger sequence lengths.

infra-oncall: kernel selection logs show fallbacks to slower FP16 matmul implementation on older CUDA drivers on subset of nodes (hosts a, b, c). rolling upgrade status shows those nodes still on driver 525.85.12. newer nodes have 535.x.

maeve: that matches canary routing — canary pool included older hosts because of binpack.

sanjay: ok two vectors: 1) model v2.3 triggers slow kernel path for some seq lengths, 2) binpack put canary pods on older driver hosts so tail got worse.

prod-oncall: immediate mitigation steps: 1) keep canary traffic on stable, 2) cordon affected hosts for inference scheduling, 3) plan rollback of v2.3 rollout once we confirm repro.

infra-oncall: cordoning now:  
```
kubectl cordon gpu-a-03
kubectl cordon gpu-b-01
kubectl cordon gpu-c-02
```
pods on those nodes will be drained and rescheduled onto newer-driver nodes (may take ~2m).

maeve: tracing shows that after drain p99 sits at 1.95s — under SLO. nice.

customer-success: I told both customers we've paused the rollout and routing is back to stable; they acknowledged. I'll open a ticket for the Dedicated customer about canary placement.

sanjay: next: we should block future canary pools from landing on older-driver nodes until drivers are upgraded or we add driver-aware scheduling. add node selector label `cuda>=535` for canary-k8s affinity.

infra-oncall: creating taint/affinity rule. command we applied:  
```
kubectl label node gpu-*-* cuda_version=535
# and update deployment affinity in canary spec
```

maeve: for root cause doc: need to capture exact sequence length range that causes slow-path + model op patterns. OLAP of traces/inputs needed. I'm dumping 500 tail traces to s3: `s3://redwood-incidents/1795555555/canary-tails/`

olivia: filing an eval to run model v2.3 on a matrix of sequence lengths and drivers to reproduce: jira RI-6789.

incident-bot: NOTE: On-call handoff scheduled at 16:00Z. prod-oncall handing to sanjay for the rest of the incident.

prod-oncall: handing to sanjay — summary: paused rollout, routed to stable, cordoned older-driver nodes, scaled canary replicas up to test, observed p99 improved after drain. customers notified.

sanjay: taking it. next steps for this shift: 1) confirm driver upgrade plan for affected pools, 2) decide rollback vs fix for v2.3 (we should probably rollback until kernel path optimized), 3) postmortem. I will leave a checklist in the incident doc.

customer-success: customers asked about ETA to re-enable canary — they want a timeline. we'll coordinate once you decide rollback vs patch.

maeve: we're leaning rollback for immediate safety. rollback command below:  
```
redwoodctl rollout rollback --env=prod --from=canary-v2 --to=stable --confirm
```

infra-oncall: if we rollback, we should also add a preflight that checks driver compatibility before ramping. I'll draft a scheduler admission webhook to reject canary pods on nodes with driver <535.

sanjay: agreed. action owners: infra-oncall -> driver scheduling preflight (ETA: EOD), olivia/maeve -> repro matrix and fix/workaround (ETA: 48h), prod-oncall -> coordinate rollback and customer comms (ETA: now).

incident-bot: UPDATE: rollback executed by prod-oncall at 15:28:44Z; rollout state=stable; p99 observed=1.88s at 15:30:12Z.

maeve: collecting all artifacts for postmortem. saved logs and traces to s3 path above. please add any related slack snippets or commands to the incident doc.

sanjay: thanks team. we'll keep monitoring for 2 hours then transition to follow-up. leaving a note to schedule a deep-dive with model and runtime teams tomorrow. :thumbsup:

prod-oncall: closing active paging now, will add pager duty note and link to postmortem draft.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (page resolved) at 15:40:05Z. Postmortem owner assigned: maeve.

olivia: quick note for postmortem: root cause = interaction between model v2.3 attention kernel patterns + outdated CUDA driver on subset of canary hosts -> triggered slow-path matmul fallback -> tail latency spike. mitigation=pause+rollback+node cordon+driver-aware scheduling. follow-ups=driver upgrade, scheduler preflight, model kernel optimization.

sanjay: adding severity P1->P2 reduction in the incident doc since service restored and no customer data lost.

maeve: will draft the postmortem and include timeline, impact table, and remediation tickets.

customer-success: customers updated and happy with rollback. will keep them in the loop.

(END THREAD)
